name: NAPRUTI Cranberry
question: Is cranberry extract prophylaxis noninferior to trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole for preventing symptomatic recurrent urinary tract infections in premenopausal women?

arms.label: Cranberry extract capsules 500 mg twice daily

design.population: 221 community-dwelling premenopausal women aged at least 18 years with at least three self-reported symptomatic urinary tract infections in the preceding year.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, double-dummy noninferiority randomized trial
design.locator: JAMA full text, Methods (Patients, Intervention); Results (Participant flow); Table 1

verdictNote: Cranberry failed the prespecified noninferiority margin; TMP-SMX increased E. coli resistance.
takeaway: In premenopausal women with recurrent UTI, cranberry extract capsules produced more symptomatic recurrences than daily trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole over 12 months (4.0 versus 1.8 per woman); the 2.2-episode mean difference failed the prespecified 1.3-episode noninferiority margin. TMP-SMX increased E. coli resistance.

reports.label: 12-month randomized report
reports.citation: Beerepoot MAJ, ter Riet G, Nys S, et al. "Cranberries vs Antibiotics to Prevent Urinary Tract Infections: A Randomized Double-blind Noninferiority Trial in Premenopausal Women." *Arch Intern Med.* 2011;171(14):1270-1278. doi:10.1001/archinternmed.2011.306
reports.followUp: 12 months of prophylaxis plus 3 months after discontinuation
reports.followUpLocator: JAMA full text, Methods (Assessments, Outcome measures); Table 2

results.measure: Mean symptomatic episodes per woman during 12 months; mean difference, cranberry minus TMP-SMX
results.note: Noninferiority required the upper 95% confidence limit of the cranberry-minus-TMP-SMX difference to be below 1.3 episodes. Means were adjusted for selective dropout by inverse probability of censoring weighting; catheter users were excluded.
results.locator: JAMA full text, Methods (Statistical analysis); Results (Primary outcomes); Table 2 and Figure 2A

results.measure: 12-month Kaplan–Meier estimated proportion with a clinical recurrence
results.note: Prespecified primary clinical outcome; no separate noninferiority threshold was specified. Percentages are Kaplan–Meier estimates, not crude numerators divided by analysis n.
results.locator: JAMA full text, Results (Primary outcomes); Table 2 and footnote c

results.measure: Median months to first clinical recurrence
results.note: Prespecified primary clinical outcome; P value from log-rank test; no separate noninferiority threshold was specified.
results.locator: JAMA full text, Results (Primary outcomes); Table 2 and Figure 2B

results.endpoint: TMP-SMX resistance in fecal E. coli
results.measure: Resistant isolates after 1 month of prophylaxis
results.note: Prespecified primary resistance outcome; the text reports isolate percentages without isolate numerators or denominators for this timepoint.
results.locator: JAMA full text, Abstract (Results); Results (Primary outcomes); Figure 3

results.endpoint: TMP-SMX resistance in asymptomatic-bacteriuria E. coli
results.measure: Resistant urinary isolates after 1 month of prophylaxis
results.note: Prespecified primary resistance outcome; the text reports isolate percentages without isolate numerators or denominators for this timepoint.
results.locator: JAMA full text, Abstract (Results); Results (Primary outcomes); Figure 3

results.measure: Indigenous E. coli resistance 3 months after discontinuation of prophylaxis

values.ctl: returned to baseline 3 months after TMP-SMX discontinuation

results.note: The article does not provide a pooled percentage for this post-treatment comparison.
results.locator: JAMA full text, Abstract (Results); Results (Primary outcomes); Figure 3

results.measure: Mean episodes per woman during 12 months
results.note: Means adjusted for selective dropout; symptomatic episodes required bacteriuria as well as clinical symptoms.
results.locator: JAMA full text, Methods (Outcome measures); Table 2 and footnote b

harms.label: Any adverse event during prophylaxis
harms.note: Safety population was 109 cranberry and 98 TMP-SMX recipients.

harms.label: Adverse event leading to withdrawal
harms.note: Masked safety board judged treatment relation likely for 5/109 (4.6%) and 5/98 (5.1%), respectively.

harms.label: Serious adverse event
harms.locator: JAMA full text, Table 4; Results (Adverse events)
harms.note: One TMP-SMX recipient had treatment-related Stevens–Johnson syndrome and withdrew; none in the cranberry arm had a treatment-related serious adverse event.

values.exp: Cran-Max cranberry extract 500 mg twice daily plus nightly placebo tablet for 12 months
values.ctl: TMP-SMX 480 mg nightly plus placebo capsule twice daily for 12 months

delivery.label: Cranberry type A proanthocyanidin content
delivery.value: 9.1 mg/g extract, measured by high-performance liquid chromatography; two 500 mg capsules supplied approximately 9.1 mg/day.

delivery.label: Urinary antibiotic activity during TMP-SMX prophylaxis
delivery.value: 632/722 urine samples (87.5%) showed antibacterial activity; cranberry adherence was not directly measured.
delivery.locator: JAMA full text, Results (Compliance with TMP-SMX); Comment

delivery.label: Antibiotic prescriptions for symptomatic UTI
delivery.locator: JAMA full text, Results (Antibiotic consumption and other infections)

reports.label: 12-month economic evaluation
reports.citation: Bosmans JE, Beerepoot MAJ, Prins JM, et al. "Cost-Effectiveness of Cranberries vs Antibiotics to Prevent Urinary Tract Infections in Premenopausal Women: A Randomized Clinical Trial." *PLoS One.* 2014;9(4):e91939. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0091939
reports.followUp: 12-month economic analysis of the same randomized cohort
reports.followUpLocator: PLOS One PDF pp1–2, Abstract and Materials and Methods (Design, Outcome measures)

results.measure: Mean total cost in 2009 euros; mean difference, cranberry minus TMP-SMX
results.note: Costs were multiply imputed; the analysis omitted downstream costs of antibiotic resistance.
results.locator: PLOS One PDF p6, Table 3; pp4–5, Costs and Discussion

results.measure: Multiply imputed mean episodes over 12 months; mean difference, cranberry minus TMP-SMX
results.note: Different imputation method and analysis cohort from the 2011 primary report; this is a reanalysis, not a new follow-up cohort.
results.locator: PLOS One PDF p6, Table 3; p4, Clinical outcomes; p5, Discussion

relations.note: The linked NAPRUTI trial compared oral lactobacilli with TMP-SMX in postmenopausal women.
